title_pattern.notes: No hook at all: the caption is just two character-name hashtags (Chen Jie is the narrator boy), the series tag a repost account uses so followers can find more episodes. It gets channel-median views, a good baseline: the video itself carries all the hook work. Our titles should NOT copy this; outliers in this niche use a one-line premise (e.g. 'On the train I saw a long-armed monster').

thumbnail.composition: Auto cover = the first frame of the video. Letterboxed landscape picture in the middle third of a 9:16 black frame. Boy in a neon-yellow jacket centre-left, medium shot, staring at camera with huge round black-ringed eyes; dad behind him at right, smirking; train window with night hills at left.
thumbnail.colours: Dominant neon yellow-green jacket against grey/brown/navy interior and heavy black bars; skin tones flat beige; overall dark with one loud colour.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Low: two characters at similar scale, each about half the picture height, and the picture is only ~40% of the frame because of the bars. The expression contrast (terrified kid vs grinning dad) is the only tension.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Mostly it doesn't, which suits a control. TikTok's For You feed autoplays, so the cover matters little. The neon jacket and the uncanny saucer eyes make the frame readable at small size, and the scared kid next to a smiling adult hints that something is off. For our videos, a text overlay with the premise and a full-bleed 9:16 frame would do better.

hook.verbatim_0_to_5s: On the train, I saw a long-armed monster. It waved at me through the fog. As I wondered what it was, Dad went pale.
hook.verbatim_5_to_12s: Dad trembled and told Mom, "It's here." "What's here?" "That thing. It's here! It's on the mountain, watching us."
hook.device: In medias res, first-person sighting. The monster is named by its one wrong body part ('long-armed') and does something friendly-but-wrong (it waves). It cuts straight to an adult's fear reaction, which tells the viewer the threat is real and has a history ('it's been over ten years'). Three open loops in under 20 s: what is it, why does dad know it, why now.
hook.visual_0_5s: 0-0.6 s boy and dad two-shot (cover frame); 0.6-3.5 s dark navy night sky, black mountain ridge, tiny long-armed silhouette on the peak (the only 'monster' image for the first minute); 3.5-5.6 s back on the boy, slow pan to dad's face draining. Captions in white at the bottom of the picture band from frame 1.

beats.summary: First-person sighting line over a night-mountain silhouette: a long-armed monster waved at me through the fog.
Dad goes pale ('It's here'), mom remembers; reveal there is a history: 'it's been over ten years, how could it find us?'
Mom looks and sees nothing, dad insists, looks again and freezes, then mom sees it too: 'We're doomed... why is it still hunting us?'
Boy asks what it is; dad: don't ask, can't say its name or it will remember our voices (lore rule).
It is closer and looks human; a landslide has stopped the train until tomorrow; family decides to move cars.
Crowded car, dad relaxes: it can't break the train, once we move we're safe; mom silent.
Ryan from their village screams at his phone: his parents were found as drained empty skins; passengers guess a bear; parents silent; boy blurts 'did that thing do this?'
Ryan's earlier photo of his parents waving goodbye has a blurry long-armed figure in the corner; passenger debate dismantles the bear theory (hibernating, arms longer than legs).
Parents hide the truth: it tracks Ryan's scent, so Ryan is bait that keeps the family alive. Time skip to 9 pm, they relax.
Something heavy lands on the roof and walks; a man sticks his head out the window, his body shrinks to an empty skin.
Train police fire at the roof, silence returns; dad says bullets can't hurt it and it can control minds.
Bowl-sized glowing eyes stare at the boy through the window; later a hand strokes his head as he sleeps, mom says she didn't touch him.
A pushed boulder smashes the car, a hairy hand drags a passenger out; police insist nobody is missing.
Dad: it broke the train on purpose, we're the target. Passengers and Ryan flee into the dark; family stays.
Boy suddenly remembers Ryan died years ago (he went to the funeral feast); parents freeze, deny, ignore him; 'someone must be under its control'.
Cuts off mid-story: download Yanyan Stories, search 'Fog Creature' for the ending (app-funnel repost).

pacing.re_hook_interval_s: new threat or reveal roughly every 30-45 s (monster sighting 0, confirmation 37, closer 61, victim 114, photo figure 158, secret 199, roof 223, kill 255, eyes 302, head stroke 326, boulder 337, twist 394)
pacing.notes: Very fast, wall-to-wall narration (~214 wpm) with no pauses or music beats; dialogue and narration in the same voice, so lines alternate 'Dad said X' and quoted speech. Visual pace is slow: most shots are 3-15 s two-shots with a constant slow push-in or pan, mouth flaps and expression swaps carrying the change. Rare inserts (phone photo, eyes in window, boulder) are the visual peaks.
pacing.shot_list_note: 48 entries; long dialogue stretches with alternating two-shots are grouped into one entry (e.g. 196-230 s).

techniques_worth_copying: Wrong-body-part monster naming: one physical anomaly ('long-armed', 'bowl-sized eyes', 'arms longer than legs') repeated as the creature's identity. Easy to draw as an SVG silhouette.
Adult-fear validation: the child sees it, but the parent's recognition ('it's been over ten years') is the real hook, because it creates backstory without exposition.

Lore rules spoken as warnings: 'can't say its name or it will remember our voices', 'tracks by scent', 'bullets can't hurt it', 'controls minds'. Each rule is a cheap re-hook and sets up later payoffs.
Contained setting plus a trap: a train stopped by a landslide until morning. It is one background set, reused for 7 minutes.
Evidence-in-a-photo insert: zoom into the corner of a phone photo to reveal the blurry figure. That is code-friendly (a rect frame, a blur filter, a push-in) and makes a strong mid-video peak.
Moral rot: the parents knowingly let an innocent be bait. The family-secret dilemma keeps viewers judging and commenting.
Authority gaslighting: police insist 'no passenger is missing' after everyone saw someone dragged out. That builds dread through denial.
Personal micro-scares between set pieces: eyes in the window, and a hand stroking the head while mom says 'I didn't touch you'.
Memory twist near the end: the friendly victim was dead years ago. It reframes everything and sets up the next part.
Hard cliffhanger + 'search X to see the ending' end card. For us: 'Part 2' or 'follow for the ending' instead of an app funnel.
Wall-to-wall caption track: one sentence per cue, white sans at the bottom, from frame 1, so it can be watched muted.

code_only_remake_requirements.feasibility: High. The visual language is limited 2D puppet animation: static backgrounds, characters as rigid cutouts with swappable mouths, eyes and blush layers, and a slow camera move on every shot. All of it is reproducible in Remotion with SVG character rigs. The creature is only ever a silhouette, eyes, a hand or a hairy black mass, which is ideal for code.
assets: 1 night-exterior SVG: gradient navy sky, layered black mountain ridges, fog gradient band, parametric long-armed silhouette (arm length and pose as props)
2 train-interior backgrounds: seat row with brown seats and a blue-framed window (night-hill parallax inside the window), and a grey aisle with a row of seats for wide shots

Character rigs (4-6): flat-colour chibi-proportion bodies, big head, pose variants (sit, stand, point, hold phone); face layers for eyes (normal, saucer/black-ringed fear, closed), mouths (closed, open, talk 3 frames), purple under-eye fear shading and blush toggles

Inserts: phone-photo frame (red brick wall yard, victims as flattened 'empty skin' shapes), photo-corner blur zoom, glowing ringed eyes in a black window (radial gradients + glow filter), shadow hand, boulder + jagged black hole mask, hairy spiky silhouette (noise-displaced path)
End card: 'search' pill sticker (red tab + white field) with series title
components: LetterboxFrame or full-bleed 9:16 option (we should go full-bleed; the letterbox is a repost artifact)
KenBurns camera: per-shot slow push-in/pan with easing; optional shake on impacts
CharacterRig with lip-flap driven by TTS word timings and expression keyframes
Shot sequencer from storyboard JSON: shot type, characters, expression and camera per caption cue (~1 shot per 2-3 cues)
Caption track: one sentence per cue, white sans with dark outline, bottom-centre of the picture
Insert/overlay components: PhonePhoto, GlowEyes, ShadowHand, ImpactHole
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Single local TTS voice (Kokoro) reading narration and dialogue at ~200-215 wpm with no gaps; low drone bed; SFX for the roof slam, gunshots and the boulder crash (synth/noise-generated or CC0).
code_only_remake_requirements.typography: Clean geometric sans (Montserrat/Inter Medium), white, ~3.2% of picture width, thin black stroke/shadow, max 2 lines, centred.
code_only_remake_requirements.timing_data: ~215 caption cues over 7 min (avg 1.9 s), ~80 shots (avg ~5 s), a re-hook every 30-45 s, cold-open monster image within the first second, cliffhanger in the last 5 s.
